name: How do contractors drywall around basement ductwork and support beams?

mainEntity.name: How do contractors drywall around basement ductwork and support beams?

acceptedAnswer.text: Basement ductwork, structural steel posts, and low-hanging pipes are enclosed using custom-framed wood boxes called soffits or chases before drywall is applied. An experienced finish contractor frames tight bulkheads around duct runs to maximize remaining ceiling height while preserving clean lines. Drywall is then measured, cut, and fastened around the framing with metal or composite corner bead to protect outside edges from dents. If access to valves or cleanouts is necessary, your contractor can frame neat openings fitted with removable access panels rather than sealing them permanently.
acceptedAnswer.description: Contractors build framed wood soffits around ducts and beams, then hang drywall and install durable corner beads for clean, protected edges.
